Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at the data patterns:

## Example 1 (2024-08-06)
- History: Price started around 68.52 and drifted up to 71.17, then 70.44
- Sentiment: Mixed, ending with 0.00
- Model forecast: Started at 69.54, gradually increasing to 73.98
- True outcome: Started at 69.96, gradually increasing to 73.98... wait that's the same? Let me look more carefully.

Actually looking at this more carefully - the model forecasts and true outcomes in Example 1 appear to be very similar from day 4-9, but diverge after that. Let me look at the divergence pattern.

Looking at Example 1 more carefully:
- Model: [69.54, 69.88, 70.03, 68.85, 71.27, 69.79, 70.14, 70.28, 70.66, 71.36, 71.63, 70.98, 70.50, 70.31, 69.84, 70.91, 70.33, 70.94, 70.61, 71.19, 69.53, 69.14, 69.21, 70.42, 71.37, 70.75, 73.27, 73.50, 74.39, 73.98]

The model is consistently UNDERFORECASTING prices after about day 4-5. The true prices are higher than the model forecasts.
